comment: The consumer's auth tunables — the project's OWN reviewed values for the keys tools/auth-posture.json declares tunable, each inside the bound that file holds. This file is SEEDED (yours to retune; `update` never clobbers it) and write-guard-protected: a retune is a reviewed human commit, and tools/check-auth-posture.mjs holds the closure three ways — config.toml must equal the row, the row must sit inside the owned bound, and every declared tunable must have a row. `additionalSections` is the same split applied to the section census: a consumer who enables a surface section ([realtime], [storage], [functions.<name>]) records it here with a why, and the census unions it with the owned core — a section neither register names still reds. The seeded values below are the template's own; retuning is editing this file and config.toml in one diff, which is the two-place act that makes the change reviewable.

auth.jwt_expiry.why: One hour — the template default. Long enough that a mobile session survives ordinary use between refreshes; short enough that a stolen access token dies the same afternoon. Retune inside the owned 300..86400 bound with the trade written here.

auth.enable_signup.why: Self-service signup is on — the scaffold is a product skeleton and a signup path is part of the worked example. An invite-only deployment flips this with its reasoning in this row.

auth.email.enable_signup.why: Email/password is the scaffold's worked signup channel (the sign-in exemplar uses it). A deployment moving to OAuth-only flips this here.

auth.email.enable_confirmations.why: LOCAL-ONLY FALSE: `supabase start` must give a usable account without a round trip through Mailpit. The DEPLOYED project must have confirmations ON — the [remotes] blocks or the Dashboard own that value, and no local gate can see it; this row is where that trade stays written.

auth.mfa.max_enrolled_factors.why: The CLI default ceiling. Lowering it is a legitimate product tightening (one factor per user is a real posture); the owned bound refuses zero, which would disable enrolment while the totp floor claims it works.
